raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

`ModelOptNvFp4FusedMoEMethod.process_weights_after_loading` rewrites the FP4 expert tensors in place for the selected backend:

- `flashinfer_trtllm` (SM100): each expert's `w13_weight` / `w2_weight` rows are shuffled, and the block scales are row-shuffled and then interleaved with `nvfp4_block_scale_interleave`;
- `flashinfer_cutlass` (SM120): the block scales are swizzled into `w13_weight_scale` / `w2_weight_scale` themselves (`alias_or_bind_derived_param`).

A weight-update session (`begin_weight_update` -> `update_weights_from_tensor` / `update_weights_from_distributed` -> `end_weight_update`) post-processes **every** MoE layer at the end, but `ModelOptNvFp4FusedMoEMethod` has no `restore_weights_before_loading`. Any update that does not rewrite every expert tensor of every MoE layer therefore permutes the untouched experts a second time. The engine keeps serving with corrupted MoE weights and reports success. Full reloads from disk are unaffected, because they rewrite everything before post-processing.

## Modifications

- `ModelOptNvFp4FusedMoEMethod.restore_weights_before_loading` undoes the repack in place (same storage, so captured CUDA graphs stay valid). Restore followed by post-processing is the identity on experts the update does not rewrite, so any subset of tensors or experts can be updated.
  - TRT-LLM: `restore_fp4_moe_weights_from_flashinfer_trtllm` inverts the row permutations (from FlashInfer's cached permute indices, checked to be bijections) and the scale interleave. FlashInfer has no inverse for `nvfp4_block_scale_interleave`; the kernel only moves bytes, so the inverse is recovered by running it on the bytes of each element's flat index (one call per byte plane, cached per shape).
  - CUTLASS: `unswizzle_blockscale` (the inverse of `swizzle_blockscale`) when the swizzled scale is aliased onto the checkpoint scale.
  - The restore is all-or-nothing: every permutation for w13 and w2 is built and checked before any byte moves, and the layer is marked restored only after the copies. A failed check raises and leaves the layer unchanged. The copies run one expert at a time, so the temporaries stay at one expert's size while the KV cache is resident.
- `process_weights_after_loading` tags a layer as restorable only when the repack is an exact byte permutation. Restore stays a no-op, which is the current behaviour, for padded TRT-LLM layouts (padded weights, or block scales whose rows are not a multiple of 128 or whose columns are not a multiple of 4, which the scale interleave pads), clamped-SwiGLU checkpoints whose w13 E4M3 scales get rescaled, interleaved-w13 checkpoints, and the CuteDSL, Marlin and MegaMoE paths; a weight update that meets such a layer logs a one-time warning.
- Tests:
  - `test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_modelopt_nvfp4_moe_restore.py` runs the real post-processing for both backends and checks that restore returns the checkpoint bytes in the same storage, that a partial update leaves the other experts bit-identical and equal to a fresh load, and that restore is a no-op before post-processing and when repeated. It also checks that a restore whose permutation check fails leaves the layer unchanged, and that block scales the interleave or swizzle pads (hidden size 192) are not marked restorable on TRT-LLM and keep their checkpoint copy on CUTLASS.
  - `test/registered/rl/test_update_weights_from_tensor_nvfp4_moe.py` serves `nvidia/Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4` and checks with `/weights_checker` `raw_checksum` that same-bytes updates of a dense tensor, and of one expert of one layer, leave every expert parameter bit-identical.

## Accuracy Tests

Bitwise check, `nvidia/Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4` on 1x GB200 (`flashinfer_trtllm`, auto), main = `8d4e1ce4c7`. `/weights_checker` `raw_checksum` (sha256 of each parameter's raw bytes) over the expert parameters before and after `begin_weight_update` -> `update_weights_from_tensor` with the checkpoint's own bytes -> `end_weight_update` (the new e2e test):

| Update | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `model.norm.weight` only | 192 expert params changed | 0 changed |
| expert 0 of layer 0 (12 tensors) | 192 expert params changed | 0 changed |

192 = 48 MoE layers x {`w13_weight`, `w13_weight_scale`, `w2_weight`, `w2_weight_scale`}: on main, a weight update that does not touch any expert still corrupts every MoE layer.

The same check on 1x RTX PRO 6000 (SM120, `--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutlass`), where only the block scales are repacked: main 96 expert params changed (48 MoE layers x {`w13_weight_scale`, `w2_weight_scale`}) for each update, this PR 0. On 1x GB300 (`flashinfer_trtllm`) the result matches GB200: main 192 changed, this PR 0.

The new unit test fails on main (6 of 6 backend subtests) and passes on GB200, GB300 and RTX PRO 6000. Serving outputs are unchanged by construction: the hook only runs inside a weight-update session. 

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No runtime change: restore runs only inside a weight-update session, and serving kernels and layouts are unchanged.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). Not needed: no new flag, env var or user-facing behaviour beyond the fix.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). Accuracy: bitwise weight checks above. Speed: no serving-path change.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

Prepared with the help of Claude Code; every result above was measured as described.

3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.

     )
+    # nvfp4_block_scale_interleave pads scale rows to 128 and columns to 4.

+        w13_weight.shape != layer.w13_weight.shape
+        or w2_weight.shape != layer.w2_weight.shape
+        or any(
+            scale.shape[-2] % 128 or scale.shape[-1] % 4
+            for scale in (w13_weight_scale, w2_weight_scale)

     (
         gemm1_weights_fp4_shuffled,
@@ -714,6 +723,115 @@ def align_fp4_moe_weights_for_flashinfer_trtllm(
     layer.intermediate_size_per_partition = intermediate_size
 
 
+def _fp4_block_scale_interleave_sources(
+    shape: torch.Size, device: torch.device
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Source position of every output byte of ``nvfp4_block_scale_interleave``.
+
+    The kernel only moves bytes, so running it on the bytes of each element's
+    flat index recovers the permutation without restating its layout here.
+    """
+    from flashinfer import nvfp4_block_scale_interleave
+
+    numel = shape.numel()
+    positions = torch.arange(numel, device=device, dtype=torch.int64)
+    sources = torch.zeros(numel, device=device, dtype=torch.int64)
+    shift = 0
+    while (numel - 1) >> shift:
+        plane = ((positions >> shift) & 0xFF).to(torch.uint8).view(shape)
+        moved = nvfp4_block_scale_interleave(plane).reshape(-1)
+        sources |= moved.to(torch.int64) << shift
+        shift += 8
+    if not torch.equal(sources.sort().values, positions):
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            f"nvfp4_block_scale_interleave is not a permutation for shape "
+            f"{tuple(shape)}; the TRT-LLM scale layout cannot be undone."
+        )
+    return sources
+
+
+def _inverse_permutation(indices: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    if not torch.equal(
+        indices.sort().values,
+        torch.arange(indices.numel(), device=indices.device),
+    ):
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            "flashinfer TRT-LLM row permutation is not a bijection, so the "
+            "FP4 MoE layout cannot be undone for a weight update."
+        )
+    return torch.argsort(indices)
+
+
+def restore_fp4_moe_weights_from_flashinfer_trtllm(
+    layer: Module, cache_permute_indices: dict
+) -> None:
+    """Undo the shuffles of ``align_fp4_moe_weights_for_flashinfer_trtllm`` in place.
+
+    Every step is a byte permutation, so restoring and aligning again leaves
+    experts that a weight update does not rewrite bit-identical. Only for
+    layouts that needed no padding. Every permutation is built and checked
+    before any byte moves, so a failed check leaves the layer as it was.
+    """
+    from flashinfer.fused_moe.core import (
+        _maybe_get_cached_w3_w1_permute_indices,
+        get_w2_permute_indices_with_cache,
+    )
+
+    epilogue_tile_m = 128
+    is_gated = layer.moe_runner_config.is_gated
+    plans = []
+    for weight_name, scale_name in (
+        ("w13_weight", "w13_weight_scale"),
+        ("w2_weight", "w2_weight_scale"),
+    ):
+        weight = getattr(layer, weight_name).data.view(torch.uint8)
+        scale = getattr(layer, scale_name).data.view(torch.uint8)
+        if weight_name == "w13_weight":
+            weight_indices = _maybe_get_cached_w3_w1_permute_indices(
+                cache_permute_indices,
+                weight[0],
+                epilogue_tile_m,
+                is_gated_act_gemm=is_gated,
+            )
+            scale_indices = _maybe_get_cached_w3_w1_permute_indices(
+                cache_permute_indices,
+                scale[0],
+                epilogue_tile_m,
+                num_elts_per_sf=16,
+                is_gated_act_gemm=is_gated,
+            )
+        else:
+            weight_indices = get_w2_permute_indices_with_cache(
+                cache_permute_indices, weight[0], epilogue_tile_m
+            )
+            scale_indices = get_w2_permute_indices_with_cache(
+                cache_permute_indices, scale[0], epilogue_tile_m, num_elts_per_sf=16
+            )
+
+        sources_key = ("fp4_block_scale_interleave", tuple(scale.shape[1:]))
+        sources = cache_permute_indices.get(sources_key)
+        if sources is None:
+            sources = _fp4_block_scale_interleave_sources(scale[0].shape, scale.device)
+            cache_permute_indices[sources_key] = sources
+        plans.append(
+            (
+                weight,
+                _inverse_permutation(weight_indices.to(weight.device)),
+                scale,
+                sources,
+                _inverse_permutation(scale_indices.to(scale.device)),
+            )
+        )
+
+    # One expert at a time keeps the temporaries to a single expert's size.
+    for weight, weight_inverse, scale, sources, scale_inverse in plans:
+        permuted_rows = torch.empty_like(scale[0])
+        for expert in range(weight.shape[0]):
+            weight[expert].copy_(weight[expert][weight_inverse])
+            permuted_rows.view(-1)[sources] = scale[expert].reshape(-1)
+            scale[expert].copy_(permuted_rows[scale_inverse])
+
+
 def get_activation_type(activation: str, is_gated: bool = True) -> int:
     """Map SGLang activation string to FlashInfer ActivationType int value."""
     from flashinfer.fused_moe.core import ActivationType

     per_tensor_dequantize,

 )
 from sglang.srt.layers.radix_attention import RadixAttention
 from sglang.srt.layers.utils import alias_or_bind_derived_param, copy_or_rebind_param

     def process_weights_after_loading(self, layer: torch.nn.Module) -> None:
         """Transform packed FP4 MoE weights and scales for the selected backend."""

         if getattr(layer, "inference_moe_w13_interleaved", False) and not getattr(
             layer, "_w13_deinterleaved", False

@@ -2845,6 +2848,7 @@ def _slice_scale(w):

             runner_config = layer.moe_runner_config
             is_situ = runner_config.activation == "situ"
@@ -2868,6 +2872,7 @@ def _slice_scale(w):
                     block_scales.copy_(
                         block_scales.float().mul_(ratios[:, :, None, None])
                     )
+                    w13_scales_rescaled = True
                     copy_or_rebind_param(layer, "g1_alphas", shared_alphas)
                     copy_or_rebind_param(layer, "g1_alphas_up", shared_alphas)
                 copy_or_rebind_param(
@@ -2973,6 +2978,12 @@ def _slice_scale(w):
             # placeholders from create_weights.
             layer.w13_blockscale_swizzled = layer.w13_weight_scale
             layer.w2_blockscale_swizzled = layer.w2_weight_scale
+            # Exact restore needs unrescaled E4M3 scales and the standard
+            # aligner without padding (it records whether it padded).
+            if not w13_scales_rescaled and not getattr(
+                layer, "trtllm_fp4_layout_padded", True
+            ):
+                layer._fp4_moe_repack = "trtllm"
 
         else:
             # CUTLASS processing - handle w13 and w2 separately
@@ -3051,6 +3062,9 @@ def _slice_scale(w):
                 w2_blockscale_swizzled,
             )
 
+            if self.enable_flashinfer_cutlass_moe and not intermediate_size_pad:
+                layer._fp4_moe_repack = "cutlass"
+
             if self._is_cutedsl_v2_standard:
                 # CuteDSL v2 only: convert blockscales to MMA layout for
                 # CuteDslMoEWrapper.  The v1 (deepep) path uses the
@@ -3097,6 +3111,46 @@ def _slice_scale(w):
                 if layer._cutedsl_wrapper is not None:
                     refresh_cutedsl_standard_scales_for_weight_update(layer)
 
+    def restore_weights_before_loading(self, layer: torch.nn.Module) -> None:
+        """Undo the in-place FP4 repack before a weight update.
+
+        `process_weights_after_loading` permutes weights and block scales in
+        place, so running it again on experts an update did not rewrite would
+        permute them twice. Restoring the checkpoint layout first keeps those
+        experts bit-identical.
+        """
+        if not hasattr(layer, "_fp4_moe_repack"):
+            # Not post-processed since loading or the last restore.
+            return
+        repack = layer._fp4_moe_repack
+        if repack is None or getattr(layer, "inference_moe_w13_interleaved", False):
+            logger.warning_once(
+                "This NVFP4 MoE layout cannot be restored before a weight update: "
+                "experts the update does not rewrite are post-processed twice. "
+                "Update every expert tensor, or serve with --moe-runner-backend "
+                "flashinfer_trtllm or flashinfer_cutlass."
+            )
+            return
+        if repack == "trtllm":
+            from sglang.srt.layers.moe.moe_runner.flashinfer_trtllm import (
+                restore_fp4_moe_weights_from_flashinfer_trtllm,

+"""Partial weight updates must not disturb the NVFP4 MoE experts they skip.
+
+end_weight_update post-processes every MoE layer, and NVFP4 MoE post-processing
+permutes FP4 weights and block scales in place. Pushing the checkpoint's own
+bytes for a few tensors must therefore leave every expert parameter
+bit-identical, including the MoE layers and experts the update did not touch.
+The /weights_checker raw_checksum action hashes each parameter's raw bytes.
+"""
+
+import json
+import os
+import unittest
+from typing import List, Tuple
+
+import requests
+import torch
+from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download
+from safetensors import safe_open
+
+from sglang.srt.utils import MultiprocessingSerializer, get_device_sm, kill_process_tree
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import (
+    DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_FOR_SERVER_LAUNCH,
+    DEFAULT_URL_FOR_TEST,
+    CustomTestCase,
+    popen_launch_server,
+)
+
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=240, stage="nightly", runner_config="1-gpu-small")
+
+_MODEL_NAME = "nvidia/Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4"
+_EXPERT_PREFIX = "model.layers.0.mlp.experts.0"
+_EXPERT_TENSORS = [
+    f"{_EXPERT_PREFIX}.{proj}.{suffix}"
+    for proj in ("gate_proj", "up_proj", "down_proj")
+    for suffix in ("weight", "weight_scale", "weight_scale_2", "input_scale")
+]
+
+
+def _checkpoint_tensors(names: List[str]) -> List[Tuple[str, torch.Tensor]]:
+    path = snapshot_download(_MODEL_NAME, allow_patterns=["*.json", "*.safetensors"])
+    with open(os.path.join(path, "model.safetensors.index.json")) as f:
+        weight_map = json.load(f)["weight_map"]
+    tensors = []
+    for name in names:
+        with safe_open(os.path.join(path, weight_map[name]), framework="pt") as f:
+            tensors.append((name, f.get_tensor(name).cuda()))
+    return tensors
+
+
+@unittest.skipIf(get_device_sm() < 100, "NVFP4 MoE requires SM100+")
+class TestUpdateWeightsFromTensorNvFp4Moe(CustomTestCase):
+    @classmethod
+    def setUpClass(cls):
+        cls.url = DEFAULT_URL_FOR_TEST
+        other_args = ["--mem-fraction-static", "0.6"]
+        if get_device_sm() >= 120:
+            # SM100 resolves auto to the TRT-LLM layout; SM120 serves CUTLASS.
+            other_args += ["--moe-runner-backend", "flashinfer_cutlass"]
+        cls.process = popen_launch_server(
+            _MODEL_NAME,
+            cls.url,
+            timeout=DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_FOR_SERVER_LAUNCH,
+            other_args=other_args,
+        )
+
+    @classmethod
+    def tearDownClass(cls):
+        kill_process_tree(cls.process.pid)
+
+    def _raw_checksums(self) -> dict:
+        resp = requests.post(
+            f"{self.url}/weights_checker", json={"action": "raw_checksum"}, timeout=600
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 200, resp.text)
+        checksums = resp.json()["ranks"][0]["checksums"]
+        return {n: h for n, h in checksums.items() if ".mlp.experts." in n}
+
+    def _update_weights(self, named_tensors: List[Tuple[str, torch.Tensor]]) -> dict:
+        begin = requests.post(f"{self.url}/begin_weight_update", json={}, timeout=120)
+        self.assertEqual(begin.status_code, 200, begin.text)
+        resp = requests.post(
+            f"{self.url}/update_weights_from_tensor",
+            json={
+                "serialized_named_tensors": [
+                    MultiprocessingSerializer.serialize(named_tensors, output_str=True)
+                ],
+                "flush_cache": True,
+            },
+            timeout=600,
+        )
+        end = requests.post(f"{self.url}/end_weight_update", json={}, timeout=600)
+        self.assertEqual(end.status_code, 200, end.text)
+        return resp.json()
+
+    def test_same_bytes_partial_updates_keep_every_expert(self):
+        before = self._raw_checksums()
+        self.assertGreater(len(before), 0)
+        cases = (
+            ("dense tensor only", ["model.norm.weight"]),
+            ("one expert of one layer", _EXPERT_TENSORS),
+        )
+        for name, tensor_names in cases:
+            with self.subTest(name=name):
+                result = self._update_weights(_checkpoint_tensors(tensor_names))
+                self.assertTrue(result["success"], result)
+                after = self._raw_checksums()
+                changed = sorted(n for n in before if before[n] != after.get(n))
+                self.assertEqual(changed, [])
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

+"""Weight updates on NVFP4 fused-MoE layers.
+
+`process_weights_after_loading` permutes FP4 weights and block scales in place
+(the TRT-LLM row shuffle and scale interleave, or the CUTLASS scale swizzle).
+A weight update post-processes every MoE layer again, so experts it does not
+rewrite must first be restored to the checkpoint layout by
+`restore_weights_before_loading`, or they end up permuted twice.
+
+These tests run the real post-processing on small, aligned shapes and check
+that restore is its exact inverse, so a partial update leaves the untouched
+experts bit-identical. Removing or breaking the restore turns them red.
+"""
+
+import unittest
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from unittest import mock
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
+
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=15, stage="base-b", runner_config="1-gpu-small")
+
+# Import modelopt_quant before flashinfer_trtllm (circular import through the
+# compressed_tensors schemes package otherwise).
+# isort: off
+from sglang.srt.layers.quantization import modelopt_quant
+from sglang.srt.layers.quantization.modelopt_quant import ModelOptNvFp4FusedMoEMethod
+
+# isort: on
+from sglang.srt.layers.moe.fused_moe_triton.layer import FusedMoE
+from sglang.srt.layers.moe.moe_runner.base import MoeRunnerConfig
+from sglang.srt.layers.moe.utils import MoeA2ABackend, MoeRunnerBackend
+from sglang.srt.runtime_context import get_flags
+from sglang.srt.utils import get_device_sm
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+NUM_EXPERTS = 4
+HIDDEN = 512
+INTERMEDIATE = 256
+REPACKED = ("w13_weight", "w13_weight_scale", "w2_weight", "w2_weight_scale")
+BACKENDS = (MoeRunnerBackend.FLASHINFER_CUTLASS, MoeRunnerBackend.FLASHINFER_TRTLLM)
+
+
+def _raw_tensors(seed, hidden=HIDDEN):
+    g = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(seed)
+
+    def u8(*shape):
+        return torch.randint(
+            0, 256, shape, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda", generator=g
+        )
+
+    rows = 2 * INTERMEDIATE
+    return {
+        "w13_weight": u8(NUM_EXPERTS, rows, hidden // 2),
+        "w13_weight_scale": u8(NUM_EXPERTS, rows, hidden // 16).view(
+            torch.float8_e4m3fn
+        ),
+        "w2_weight": u8(NUM_EXPERTS, hidden, INTERMEDIATE // 2),
+        "w2_weight_scale": u8(NUM_EXPERTS, hidden, INTERMEDIATE // 16).view(
+            torch.float8_e4m3fn
+        ),
+    }
+
+
+def _layer(raw):
+    config = MoeRunnerConfig(is_gated=True)
+    method = ModelOptNvFp4FusedMoEMethod(
+        SimpleNamespace(use_per_token_activation=False)
+    )
+    layer = FusedMoE.__new__(FusedMoE)
+    torch.nn.Module.__init__(layer)
+    layer.quant_method = method
+    layer.moe_runner_config = config
+    layer.num_local_experts = NUM_EXPERTS
+    layer.intermediate_size_per_partition = INTERMEDIATE
+    layer.dispatcher = SimpleNamespace(set_quant_config=lambda config: None)
+    params = {name: t.clone() for name, t in raw.items()}
+    params.update(
+        w13_weight_scale_2=torch.full((NUM_EXPERTS, 2), 0.01, device="cuda"),
+        w2_weight_scale_2=torch.full((NUM_EXPERTS,), 0.01, device="cuda"),
+        w13_input_scale=torch.full((NUM_EXPERTS, 2), 0.5, device="cuda"),
+        w2_input_scale=torch.full((NUM_EXPERTS,), 0.5, device="cuda"),
+    )
+    for name, data in params.items():
+        layer.register_parameter(name, torch.nn.Parameter(data, requires_grad=False))
+    if not method.enable_flashinfer_trtllm_moe:
+        for name in ("w13", "w2"):
+            setattr(
+                layer,
+                f"{name}_blockscale_swizzled",
+                torch.nn.Parameter(
+                    modelopt_quant.swizzle_blockscale(params[f"{name}_weight_scale"]),
+                    requires_grad=False,
+                ),
+            )
+    return layer
+
+
+def _bytes(layer, name):
+    return getattr(layer, name).data.view(torch.uint8).clone()
+
+
+@unittest.skipIf(
+    not torch.cuda.is_available() or get_device_sm() < 100,
+    "NVFP4 MoE layouts need SM100+",
+)
+class TestNvFp4MoeRestore(CustomTestCase):
+    def _backend(self, backend):
+        return get_flags().moe.override(
+            runner_backend=backend, a2a_backend=MoeA2ABackend.NONE
+        )
+
+    def _process(self, layer):
+        with mock.patch.object(
+            modelopt_quant,
+            "should_use_flashinfer_cutlass_moe_fp4_allgather",
+            return_value=False,
+        ):
+            layer.quant_method.process_weights_after_loading(layer)
+
+    def test_restore_returns_checkpoint_layout(self):
+        raw = _raw_tensors(seed=0)
+        for backend in BACKENDS:
+            with self.subTest(backend=backend.value), self._backend(backend):
+                layer = _layer(raw)
+                self._process(layer)
+                self.assertFalse(
+                    torch.equal(
+                        _bytes(layer, "w13_weight_scale"),
+                        raw["w13_weight_scale"].view(torch.uint8),
+                    )
+                )
+                storage = {n: getattr(layer, n).data_ptr() for n in REPACKED}
+                layer.quant_method.restore_weights_before_loading(layer)
+                for name in REPACKED:
+                    self.assertTrue(
+                        torch.equal(_bytes(layer, name), raw[name].view(torch.uint8)),
+                        name,
+                    )
+                    self.assertEqual(getattr(layer, name).data_ptr(), storage[name])
+
+    def test_partial_update_keeps_untouched_experts(self):
+        raw = _raw_tensors(seed=1)
+        update = _raw_tensors(seed=2)
+        updated_raw = {name: t.clone() for name, t in raw.items()}
+        for name in REPACKED:
+            updated_raw[name][1] = update[name][1]
+        for backend in BACKENDS:
+            with self.subTest(backend=backend.value), self._backend(backend):
+                layer = _layer(raw)
+                self._process(layer)
+                before = {name: _bytes(layer, name) for name in REPACKED}
+                expected = _layer(updated_raw)
+                self._process(expected)
+
+                layer.quant_method.restore_weights_before_loading(layer)
+                for name in REPACKED:
+                    getattr(layer, name).data[1] = update[name][1]
+                self._process(layer)
+
+                for name in REPACKED:
+                    after = _bytes(layer, name)
+                    for expert in (0, 2, 3):
+                        self.assertTrue(
+                            torch.equal(after[expert], before[name][expert]),
+                            f"{name} expert {expert}",
+                        )
+                    self.assertTrue(torch.equal(after, _bytes(expected, name)), name)
+
+    def test_restore_is_a_no_op_without_a_repack(self):
+        raw = _raw_tensors(seed=3)
+        for backend in BACKENDS:
+            with self.subTest(backend=backend.value), self._backend(backend):
+                layer = _layer(raw)
+                layer.quant_method.restore_weights_before_loading(layer)
+                self._process(layer)
+                layer.quant_method.restore_weights_before_loading(layer)
+                layer.quant_method.restore_weights_before_loading(layer)
+                for name in REPACKED:
+                    self.assertTrue(
+                        torch.equal(_bytes(layer, name), raw[name].view(torch.uint8))
+                    )
+
+    def test_failed_restore_leaves_the_layer_untouched(self):
+        import flashinfer.fused_moe.core as fused_moe_core
+
+        def not_a_bijection(cache, tensor, epilogue_tile_m, **kwargs):
+            return torch.zeros(tensor.shape[0], dtype=torch.int64)
+
+        with self._backend(MoeRunnerBackend.FLASHINFER_TRTLLM):
+            layer = _layer(_raw_tensors(seed=4))
+            self._process(layer)
+            before = {name: _bytes(layer, name) for name in REPACKED}
+            # w13 plans fine; w2 fails its check after that.
+            with mock.patch.object(
+                fused_moe_core, "get_w2_permute_indices_with_cache", not_a_bijection
+            ):
+                with self.assertRaises(RuntimeError):
+                    layer.quant_method.restore_weights_before_loading(layer)
+            for name in REPACKED:
+                self.assertTrue(torch.equal(_bytes(layer, name), before[name]), name)
+            self.assertEqual(layer._fp4_moe_repack, "trtllm")
+
+    def test_padded_scale_layouts(self):
+        # hidden 192: w2 block-scale rows are not a multiple of 128, so the
+        # scale interleave/swizzle pads them.
+        raw = _raw_tensors(seed=5, hidden=192)
+        update = _raw_tensors(seed=6, hidden=192)
+
+        with self._backend(MoeRunnerBackend.FLASHINFER_TRTLLM):
+            layer = _layer(raw)
+            try:
+                self._process(layer)
+            except AssertionError:
+                # FlashInfer's TRT-LLM row shuffle needs 128-row multiples, so
+                # this layout fails at load today; restore must stay off if not.
+                pass
+            self.assertTrue(layer.trtllm_fp4_layout_padded)
+            self.assertIsNone(layer._fp4_moe_repack)
+
+        # CUTLASS keeps the padded w2 swizzle in a separate buffer, so the
+        # source scale stays in checkpoint layout and a partial update works.
+        with self._backend(MoeRunnerBackend.FLASHINFER_CUTLASS):
+            updated_raw = {name: t.clone() for name, t in raw.items()}
+            for name in REPACKED:
+                updated_raw[name][1] = update[name][1]
+            layer = _layer(raw)
+            self._process(layer)
+            expected = _layer(updated_raw)
+            self._process(expected)
+            layer.quant_method.restore_weights_before_loading(layer)
+            for name in REPACKED:
+                getattr(layer, name).data[1] = update[name][1]
+            self._process(layer)
+            for name in REPACKED + ("w2_blockscale_swizzled",):
+                self.assertTrue(
+                    torch.equal(_bytes(layer, name), _bytes(expected, name)), name
+                )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
